name: aurelius
comment: The one spec. The docs, the Lair and the Ladder read it. Numbers marked assumed are ours until real runs replace them.

actions.name: map
actions.does: send one order to many children; pick the cheapest worker type expected to pass

actions.name: check
actions.does: sample replies and test them against the order's done check

actions.name: wait
actions.does: sleep until a reply, an alarm, a deadline or a budget line

actions.name: stop
actions.does: cancel children, then kill any still running after the grace period

actions.name: report
actions.does: send a summary, facts and alarms to the parent

order.means: what done looks like, in one line
the test the reply must pass
what the worker may touch; everything else is out
the fields the reply must carry
tokens, seconds and credits; the seat enforces it

reply.means: each fact with its tag and its source
anything the parent must know now
tokens, seconds and credits used; unknown is never zero

fix_loop.then: a fresh worker, one type stronger

dial.comment: relative weights; default balanced; each goal can override

reward.means: an action that does not parse scores 0
the done check passes, as far as the seat can see

reward.when: success and the task can split
reward.means: real parallel work; fades to 0 during training

metrics.means: tasks whose done check passes on a fresh check
all credits spent divided by verified successes
seat steps plus the longest child branch, per stage
wrong-fact rate a tier sends up, divided by the rate it received
planted alarms that reach the root seat
splits that do not shorten the critical path
killed seats that resume to the same result
orders that spent past their budget

baselines.means: one large worker does the whole task alone
one seat sends every item to its own medium worker; no tiers, no checks
flat fan-out, each item to the cheapest type whose skill clears the bar

check.source: assumed until fitted from real runs

safety.rules: allow, ask or deny; the last match wins

score_row.stamp_comment: spec is the first 12 hex of sha256 of the canonical spec JSON; the rest are null for rule seats and baselines
score_row.rates: error rates times (1 + rates), from -0.5 to 0.5; 0 is the spec as written
